finding_key: packages/backend/src/main.ts::raw-body capture keys off an exact `req.url` match, so any path variation (trailing slash, proxy prefix) silently yields 401 + infinite yorkie retries

verdict.reasoning: Verified against packages/backend/src/main.ts (verify hook: `req.url?.split('?',1)[0] === '/internal/yorkie/events'`) and packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49 (`if (!header || !rawBody) throw new UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature')`). Express's default non-strict, case-insensitive routing does route `/internal/yorkie/events/` to the controller while the byte-exact comparison skips rawBody capture, so the guard 401s with a misleading "missing signature" message and the feature is silently inert — the claim's mechanism is correct. Caveats: there is no `setGlobalPrefix` in main.ts so the "proxy prefix" variant needs an external rewrite, and Yorkie retries are backoff-limited rather than infinite per the PR's own docs; neither undercuts the defect. It is triggered only by an operator typing a variant URL (the documented URL works), so I rate it a robustness/minor issue rather than a happy-path break.
